question.leadin: This war ended with the Battle of Worcester in 1651.
question.text: Name this war won by the Parliamentarians. It saw troubles between King Charles I and II with the Long Parliament and Rump Parliament respectively.
question.clue: This conflict's second phase saw the defeat of Scottish forces at Preston, after which the victorious commander perpetrated the massacre at Drogheda to punish Irish supporters of his enemies.

swap.text: While returning from the Third Crusade, this king of England was captured and held for ransom by Holy Roman Emperor Henry IV.
swap.answerHtml: Richard I [or Richard the Lionheart; or Richard Coeur de Lion; prompt on “Richard” alone]
swap.clue: He offended Leopold V, the Duke of Austria, after one campaign, leading to his capture, but he was later found by his minstrel Blondel.

question.leadin: The last phase of the French Wars of religion were named for three people that bore this name.
question.text: Give this first name, which was beared by The Duke of Navarre, the Duke of Guise, and the King of France at that time. A King of England with six wives also had this name.
question.clue: The Day of the Barricades targeted a king with this name who was assassinated by Jacques Clement.

swap.leadin: The Mamluks forced this ruler to retire from Crusading by having him stabbed with an allegedly poisoned dagger.
swap.text: Name this English king, nicknamed "Longshanks," who won the Battle of Falkirk.
swap.clue: He employed James of St. George to build an "Iron Ring" that included Flint and Rhuddlan.

question.leadin: NOTE TO MODERATOR: Do not reveal the alternate answers to the first part of the bonus unless a team answers with that, as it will reveal the answer to the second part. Thanks! The Bayeux Tapestry opens with Edward the Confessor sending Harold Godwinson as an ambassador to this monarch.
question.text: Name this king, who launched the Harrying of the North campaign after the death of Robert de Comines. The Bayeux Tapestry depicts this king's victory at the Battle of Hastings.
question.answerHtml: William the Conqueror [or William I; or William the Bastard; or William of Normandy; prompt on William]
question.clue: This king ordered for a destructive campaign to gain control of Northumbria in his Harrying of the North, and he ordered for the compilation of a written record of England, the Domesday Book.

swap.leadin: The Sun is a wonderful British magazine where you can read headlines like "Freddie Starr Ate My Hamster." answer the following about their other masterpieces of journalism.
swap.text: In 1982, The Sun notoriously printed the headline "Gotcha!" after the sinking of the General Belgrano, an event during this conflict between Britain and Argentina over an archipelago off the coast of South America.
swap.clue: This conflict began when one side's troops landed on April 2, and ended when they were forced to give up the territorial capital of Port Stanley in mid-June of the same year.

question.leadin: He was anointed as a king by Pope Leo IV at the age of four.
question.text: Name this English monarch who won the decisive Battle of Ethandun against the Viking Guthrum. He is the only English monarch given the epithet "the Great."
question.clue: He adopted his former enemy Guthrum and forced his conversion to Christianity.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about a naval fleet commanded by the duke of Medonia Sodenia.
swap.text: This vice admiral under Lord Howard during the English defeat of the Armada pre-emptively shelled the port cities of Cadiz and Corunna in 1587. He circumnavigated the world between 1577 and 1580.
swap.clue: The mojito was invented during this man's victory at Cartagena de Indias, which happened before he evacuated the original Roanoke colony.

question.text: This man defeated Richard III at Bosworth field and took the crown.
question.answerHtml: Henry VII [or Henry, Earl of Richmond; prompt on Henry Tudor]
question.clue: This ruler ordered the repeal of the Titulus Regius of his predecessor, who had seized the throne by imprisoning two princes in the Tower of London.

swap.text: A Fellow of the Royal Horticultural Society, he organized a municipal bank in Birmingham while serving as its mayor. After serving as Chancellor for the Exchequer, he assumed the British Prime Ministry in 1937. For fifteen points, name this man who spoke with Hitler on three separate occasions, while trying to adhere to a policy of appeasement.
swap.clue: The polemic Guilty Men was written during his premiership and listed him first among the offenders.

question.text: The West Port murders were carried out by these two men in Edinburgh in 1828, paving the way for the 1832 Anatomy Act regulating the body trade.

swap.text: This first leader of the Labour Party died in Glasgow in 1915 while trying to organise a general strike of pacifists against World War I.

question.leadin: This politician allegedly told Winston Churchill that if he were her husband, she'd poison his tea, to which Churchill replied that if he was married to her, he'd drink it.
question.text: Name this woman, the first to take her parliamentary seat in the House of Commons. This woman founded the Cliveden Set, a club of Nazi sympathizers that pushed for appeasement.
question.answerHtml: Nancy Astor [or Nancy Witcher Astor, Viscountess Astor of Hever Castle]
question.clue: This first woman seated as a British MP. After criticizing one politician's drinking, this woman was told, "When I wake up tomorrow, I shall be sober, and you will still be ugly!"

swap.leadin: Michael Faraday described this event by saying "the feculence rolled up in clouds"
swap.text: Identify this 1858 event that led to the Houses of Parliament's curtains being soaked in lime chloride and which led Joseph Bazalgette ("BA-zuhl-JET") to introduce a large-scale civil engineering project.
swap.answerHtml: The Great Stink [accept answers referring to a Big Stink or Great Stench or similar answers referring to a big smell in the River Thames, prompt on answers referring to a smell]

question.text: This Labour PM served nonconsecutive terms in the 1960s and 70s. He avoided the Vietnam War and opposed Enoch Powell's "Rivers of Blood speech."
question.clue: This man who was succeeded as UK Prime Minister by James Callaghan.

swap.text: The three-fold order organisation of Fuller's "Nine Principles" can be traced to the cabalistic infiuence of this man. Fuller wrote The Star in the West as a study of this man's mystical poetry and edited The Equinox with him.
swap.answerHtml: Aleister Crowley [also accept Edward Alexander Crowley ]

question.text: Fred Jesson is obsessed with crosswords, to the detriment of his marriage, in the David Lean film Brief Encounter, whose screenplay was written by this playwright and based on his play Still Life. He also wrote the play Hay Fever.

swap.leadin: This historian charted the transition from a paternalistic model of the economy to one based on market forces in his 1971 article "The Moral Economy of the English Crowd in the Eighteenth Century."
swap.text: Identify this British socialist historian who sought to rescue British workers "from the enormous condescension of posterity," in his magnum opus, The Making of the English Working Class.
swap.clue: This prominent historian supported the CND. A biographer of William Morris and William Blake, this leftist wrote a work of history that sought to rescue its subjects from the "enormous condescension of posterity."

question.text: Use of the "V" sign among resistance groups was encouraged by this British organization, whose members were nicknamed the "Baker Street Irregulars" and primarily carried out sabotage operations.
question.clue: This British organisation aided the French resistance in Operation Jedburgh and were sometimes nicknamed 'the Baker Street Irregulars' or 'Churchill's Secret Army'.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a British conspiracy FTPE.
swap.text: Many of Thistlewood's revolutionary ideas were inculcated during his time as a member of this man's namesake group. He argued that parishes should control public lands in works like 1775's The Real Rights of Man.
swap.clue: This advocate of placing all land under the control of local, democratically-elected corporations that would then lease out land to tenants at low prices. He also wrote The Real Rights of Man.
